recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the published clarification in the active Workflow module source without broadening workflow guidance or deciding the later punctuation-only FHIR-44047 issue.
issue_request: FHIR-15565 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 clarification for the Workflow module roadmap. The reporter asked whether "compensating actions" meant reimbursement because the text cited account transactions and reversals; the resolution said the intended sense was a compensating transaction and recommended changing the example and/or adding wording such as "to revert a previously recorded action".
initial_application: SVN#14775, imported as git commit 1f06d7f9af8e49eee84f4c284a7af61b48a2398b, added a link from "compensating actions" to the Wikipedia compensating transaction article. It left the account-transactions example in place, so the published clarification was only partially applied.
additional_context: source/workflow-module.html is an active Workflow module page via source/hierarchy.xml and source/modules-list.html. Later source history in 887bc2383fb7b429cfafd64a46bdfc0c40c5b627 (FHIR-44047) normalized punctuation in the same sentence but did not change or supersede the FHIR-15565 meaning. Searches of Jira, Zulip, and Confluence found no contrary or broader decision.
reconciliation: Changed source/workflow-module.html to keep the compensating transaction link while replacing "e.g., account transactions and reversals" with "to revert a previously recorded action".
source_changes: source/workflow-module.html: replaced the ambiguous account-transactions example in the Developmental Roadmap with direct wording that compensating actions revert a previously recorded action.

related_jiras.note: A later source commit for this issue touched the same sentence for punctuation only; it did not change the FHIR-15565 meaning or need a separate decision here.
